reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes a system called VehicleTalk, which uses optical wireless communication and sensing for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication. The system utilizes the head/tail LED lights of vehicles to construct communication/sensing channels. The paper includes several figures, including Figure 1, which illustrates the overview of the VehicleTalk framework, and Figure 2, which shows three types of status awareness in VehicleTalk.

The system uses a combination of optical wireless communication and sensing to enable V2V communication and perception functions. The communication component uses Raptor Codes to combat packet loss, while the perception component uses a fast risk detection algorithm to detect status changes of adjacent vehicles.

The paper presents experimental results to verify the effectiveness of the proposed system. The results show that the system can achieve a goodput of 5 kbps and a sensing task with a median RE and RER below 1.6% and 10% at a distance of 5 m.

The paper proposes a novel approach to V2V communication and sensing using optical wireless communication and sensing. The system has the potential to improve traffic safety and efficiency by enabling vehicles to communicate and sense each other's status in real-time.
